ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a 50 V DC power supply, with the positive terminal on top, connected through switch S to the upper switching node; this node is connected downward through an inductor labeled 0.6 mH to the bottom common line. At the right output terminal there is a capacitor, labeled with voltage 75 V, with its upper end negative and lower end positive; beside it there is a 5 Ω resistor in parallel with this capacitor. There is a diode between the switching node and the right output node. The problem gives the switching frequency f = 10 kHz, duty cycle D = 0.6, ideal components, and negligible capacitor ripple. Reasoning: According to the method given by the problem, the voltage magnitude across the 5 Ω load is 75 V, therefore the load power is P_out = V^2/R = 75^2/5 = 1125 W. In an ideal circuit, the average input power equals the output power, so the average input current of the 50 V power supply is I_in,avg = 1125/50 = 22.5 A. Since the power supply supplies power only when switch S is on, the average source current during the on interval is I_on,avg = I_in,avg/D = 22.5/0.6 = 37.5 A. The switching period T = 1/10000 = 100 μs, and the on time T_on = 0.6T = 60 μs. During on time the inductor bears 50 V, and the rise in inductor current is ΔI = V T_on/L = 50 × 60e-6 / 0.6e-3 = 5 A. Therefore the peak source current is the average value during the on interval plus half the ripple: I_peak = 37.5 + 5/2 = 40.0 A.

method.method_draft: After describing the image topology, compute the load current magnitude from the shown capacitor/load voltage and resistor: 75 V across 5 ohm. From the text use D = 0.6 and f = 10 kHz, so the diode/inductor discharge interval is (1-D)T. Apply capacitor charge balance: the average diode current over the whole cycle must equal the 15 A load current, and the diode conducts only during OFF, so the average inductor current during OFF is the load current divided by (1-D). Next compute the inductor ripple during OFF from the shown 75 V output magnitude, L = 0.6 mH, and Toff = (1-D)/f. Since the off-interval inductor current decreases linearly from peak to valley, add half the ripple to the off-interval average to get the peak inductor current. Finally note that this same peak occurs just before switch opening, while source current equals inductor current during the ON interval, so it is the peak current drawn from the 50 V source.

图像描述：电路左侧是一个标注为 50 V 的直流电源，上方经过开关 S 接到中间开关节点。该节点向下接一个标注为 0.6 mH 的电感到底部公共节点；该节点还通过一个二极管连接到右侧输出节点。右侧输出端有一个电容和一个 5 Ω 电阻并联，电容旁标注稳态电压为 75 V，极性为上端负、下端正。

Reasoning: According to the method given by the problem, the voltage magnitude across the 5 Ω load is 75 V, therefore the load power is P_out = V^2/R = 75^2/5 = 1125 W. In an ideal circuit, the average input power equals the output power, so the average input current of the 50 V power supply is I_in,avg = 1125/50 = 22.5 A. Since the power supply supplies power only when switch S is on, the average source current during the on interval is I_on,avg = I_in,avg/D = 22.5/0.6 = 37.5 A. The switching period T = 1/10000 = 100 μs, and the on time T_on = 0.6T = 60 μs. During on time the inductor bears 50 V, and the rise in inductor current is ΔI = V T_on/L = 50 × 60e-6 / 0.6e-3 = 5 A. Therefore the peak source current is the average value during the on interval plus half the ripple: I_peak = 37.5 + 5/2 = 40.0 A.
